title: Inheritance and Witness Revisited
premise: Sable Whitlock, the reclusive coroner of Marrow Creek, has spent years solving quietly what the police dismiss as accidents, keeping their gift for reading the dead a secret. When they find the diary of missing schoolteacher Iris Vane continuing to be written weeks after her disappearance—in handwriting Sable recognizes from the town's oldest gravestone—the trail leads to Edith Marsh, the 'dead' witness whose testimony once destroyed Sable's own family. As Sable and their found family of misfits close in on Edith's hiding place, they uncover that the town's founding families buried her alive in plain sight, erasing her name from every record. In the end, Sable must choose between protecting their own anonymity and forcing Marrow Creek to witness the truth, giving testimony at last—and discovering that belonging begins with being seen.
about_author: Hazel Hartwell is the pen name of a former rural hospice worker who spent a decade listening to last words in towns too small for traffic lights. They write mysteries about people the world overlooks, from a farmhouse office shared with three opinionated cats.

chapters.title: The Diary That Kept Breathing
chapters.summary: Sable Whitlock's POV. While cataloguing an estate sale, Sable discovers Iris Vane's diary—entries dated three weeks after her disappearance, written in a hand matching inscriptions on graves older than anyone living. The emotional beat is quiet dread: Sable, who trusts the dead more than the living, realizes the dead are trying to speak through paper. They decide, against every instinct for invisibility, to investigate.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Sable and Denny Okafor, the teenage runaway Sable informally adopted. Their inquiries reveal Edith Marsh—a witness who testified against Sable's grandfather decades ago—officially dead and buried, yet her belongings keep surfacing near fresh sites. The emotional beat is loyalty strained: Denny wants to go public; Sable begs patience, fearing exposure of their own unsanctioned investigations. A break-in at the morgue warns them someone is watching.

chapters.title: What the Founding Families Buried
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, climaxing in the old Marsh homestead cellar. Sable finds Edith alive—hidden for forty years by the founding families who falsified her death to silence her testimony, now kept captive by her grandson, Councilman Marsh, as Iris's disappearance threatens exposure. The emotional beat is terror turning to fury: Sable recognizes their own erasure in Edith's. When Marsh arrives, Sable must choose silence or witness, and chooses witness—recording everything as danger closes in.

chapters.title: A Name Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Shared POV: Sable, Denny, and finally Edith herself. With Denny's evidence and the diary's final entry, Sable testifies before a state investigator, sacrificing their anonymity to give Edith back her name. Marsh is arrested; Iris is found alive, hidden by Edith's old network. The emotional beat is belonging earned: at a small graveside ceremony, the town reads Edith's name aloud, and Sable—no longer invisible—is surrounded by the family they chose.
